ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, authorised representatives, and settlement beneficiaries against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, HM Treasury OFSI (UK) Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (where applicable), OFAC SDN List (for USD clearing and US correspondent banking), Interpol notices, Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit sanctions notices, and Bermuda UN Sanctions Regulations. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members and close associates. Source of funds and source of wealth records must be obtained for every UBO holding 25% or more. Annual re-screening and event-driven re-screening are required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda Registry of Companies (Bermuda ROC) online name reservation and clearance portal; secondary filing portal: Gibraltar Companies Registry (Registrar of Companies) for any overseas company registration or trade name registration in Gibraltar
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Bermuda company names must be in Latin/Roman script using the English alphabet; no statutory transliteration doctrine is applied. All names must be legible and capable of being pronounced in English. If a non-English word is used, a certified English translation may be required by the Registrar. Gibraltar similarly requires English-script names for any locally registered branch or trade name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Bermuda Registrar of Companies rejects a proposed name, the applicant or its licensed registered agent may submit a written request for reconsideration within 14 days from the date of the rejection notice, accompanied by an explanatory submission and any required prior ministerial consent. The Registrar must respond within 21 days. If the name remains refused, the applicant may appeal to the Supreme Court of Bermuda under the Companies (Appeals) Rules. For Gibraltar name rejection in the context of an overseas company registration, a written notice of appeal must be filed with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies within 14 days, followed by a further appeal to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar. A rejected name does not bar resubmission of a materially modified and distinguishable name; no formal extension of the 30-day reservation window is available, and a fresh reservation application is required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only with material restrictions. The Bermuda Exempted Company must maintain a physical registered office in Bermuda at the address of its licensed registered agent; a PO Box or bare virtual office is not accepted. For the Gibraltar market-facing presence, a virtual office may be used if the local registered agent holds a physical address for service of process, but the Bermuda office remains the statutory seat of the company. For online automotive aftermarket parts retail (ISIC 4791), no physical stockholding or storefront is required; the virtual office model is acceptable for business operations and EMI account opening.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 12-month probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Bermuda Registrar of Companies, Bermuda Financial Intelligence Unit, or Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit is 8-10% for a low-risk standard online retail entity. The likelihood increases to approximately 15% if the company receives tax-exempt status, triggers economic substance enquiries, or exhibits CDD/AML deficiencies. Enhanced inspection probability of 25% applies if the named UBO is a PEP or if any sanctions hits arise during initial screening.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1981 of Bermuda (as amended), Part II (Incorporation of Exempted Companies), sections 4, 5A, 12, 13, 19, 25 and 26
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda Government Corporate Registry, 1st Floor, Government Administration Building, 30 Parliament Street, Hamilton HM 12, Bermuda
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association, Form 1 (Application for Incorporation), Form 3 (Statutory Declaration of Compliance), and Certificate of Name Reservation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital or authorised share capital requirement under the Companies Act 1981 (Bermuda). Shares may be issued for such consideration as the directors determine, subject to the solvency test; no statutory escrow account is required at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) The Memorandum and Articles of Association in the form attached to the minutes, having been approved by each subscriber, are adopted as the constitution of the Company. (2) The subscription to the Company’s share capital is hereby accepted, and 1,000 ordinary shares of no par value are issued to the subscriber as fully paid. (3) The registered office of the Company shall be maintained at the address located in Bermuda as stated on the Form 1. (4) [Name A] and [Name B] are appointed as the first Directors, and [Name C] as Secretary of the Company. (5) The Directors and Secretary are jointly and severally authorised to give notices and sign all documents necessary to file and record the incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry E-Services Portal, Hamilton, Bermuda
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application online via the Bermuda Corporate Registry E-Services portal, or deliver a physical application to the counter. The proposed name must include 'Limited' or 'Ltd' unless exemption is obtained. Pay the USD 50 search and reservation fee by credit card or wire transfer at time of filing.
required_dossiers: Completed Name Reservation Form
Statement of proposed corporate activities (brief description)
Engagement letter or power of attorney from the licensed Bermuda incorporation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused as misleading, offensive, or conflicting with an existing name, the applicant may file an alternative name reservation within 2 business days. A review request may be submitted in writing to the Registrar, who will provide a written decision within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies; notarisation by a Bermuda Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association in line with section 5 of the Companies Act 1981. The subscribers must execute the constitutional documents in the physical presence of a Bermuda Notary Public, who will attest the statutory declaration of due compliance. Execute the consent forms of each proposed director and secretary.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Association
Articles of Association
Statutory Declaration of Due Compliance (Form 3)
Identity evidence (passport) and proof of address of each subscriber
Consent to act as Director (Form 4) and Consent to act as Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar raises an objection to any clause in the constitutional documents as contrary to law or public policy, the documents may be re-executed with the attending notary and resubmitted with a covering note within 7 business days without additional penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry, Hamilton, Bermuda
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the executed memorandum, articles, statutory declaration, consents, and name reservation certificate electronically through E-Services or physically at the Registry counter. Ensure the registered office address in Bermuda is stated, and obtain the written consent of the registered office provider. The incorporation application is considered complete upon formal acceptance by the Registry.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Name Reservation
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Statutory Declaration of Compliance (Form 3)
Consent to act as Director (Form 4)
Consent to act as Secretary
Registered Office Address Consent from the Bermuda service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned for incomplete particulars, the applicant may remedy the defect by providing the missing information in response to the Registry's query. The review clock will restart from the date of the complete response, and no late fee will be imposed if the response is filed within 7 calendar days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Filing Fees and Stamp Duty
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Government Treasury and Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After adjudication of the application, pay the assessed registration and stamp duty fees as invoiced by the Registry. The minimum fee is calculated on the authorised capital (USD 1,275 for capital up to USD 12,000), plus an application fee of USD 120. Payment may be made by bank wire, treasurer's cheque, or E-Services payment module.
required_dossiers: Registry invoice or fee assessment letter
Remittance evidence (wire confirmation or receipt)
Authorisation from the incorporation agent to charge the agreed fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fee payment is misallocated or underpaid, the Registry will issue a corrected demand. The deficiency may be paid within 3 business days, and the incorporation process will continue without re-advertisement or penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies; Bermuda Economic Substance Office (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon confirmation of payment, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and publishes the company in the Bermuda Official Gazette. The company must then hold its first board meeting to adopt the first board resolution, appoint officers, approve the registered office, and issue share certificates. If the company will be subject to the Bermuda Economic Substance Act 2018, complete and file the Economic Substance Return within the prescribed deadline.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar
Minutes of the first board of directors meeting
Share register and share certificate counterfoils
Written consents of Directors and Secretary (already on file)
Economic Substance Return form (ESU Form) if the company is a relevant entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains clerical errors, a request for correction may be lodged under section 13 of the Companies Act 1981. If the Economic Substance Return is rejected for insufficient substance information, a revised return may be submitted to the Economic Substance Office within 15 business days, subject to any applicable penalty waiver.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure e-commerce; the entity does not operate an industrial establishment in Bermuda or Gibraltar and no industrial licence is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None - the business scope of online retail of automotive replacement parts does not require a statutory industrial or physical operating permit under Bermuda or Gibraltar law. A Gibraltar Business Licence is not triggered because no physical commercial premises or local presence is maintained.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable - the activity is online retail and does not trigger environmental impact assessment under the Bermuda Environmental Protection Act 2016 or the Gibraltar Environmental Protection Act 2009.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance thresholds for wastewater, VOCs, and hazardous waste do not apply as there are no discharges or emissions from the commercial activity. If the company later establishes warehousing or logistics operations, it must comply with the waste management and spill prevention provisions of the Bermuda Waste Management Regulations and the Gibraltar Waste Management Act 2016.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No physical workplace, warehouse, or public-accessed premises is used, so fire safety certification, structural load inspection, and occupational clearance are not required. If a physical distribution centre or warehouse is subsequently leased in Gibraltar, the tenant must obtain a Fire Safety Certificate from the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service and a structural load compliance certificate from the Gibraltar Building Control Officer prior to occupancy, and ensure general workplace safety pursuant to the Gibraltar Health and Safety at Work Act 2000.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office under the Commissioner of Income Tax, HM Government of Gibraltar (official portal: https://www.tax.gov.gi). Overseas-company registration is administered by the Gibraltar Companies Registry / Companies and Securities Regulatory Authority (https://www.csra.gi). Gibraltar is a separate tax, customs, and VAT-administration territory from the UK.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Determine whether the Bermuda Exempted Company is resident or has a taxable establishment in Gibraltar. A company managed and controlled outside Gibraltar and having no place of business in Gibraltar is not required to register for Gibraltar income tax. 2) If a place of business is maintained, register the Bermuda Exempted Company as an overseas company with the Gibraltar Companies Registry, filing a certified copy of the Bermuda certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, Bermuda certificate of tax exemption, memorandum and articles, and details of the Gibraltar registered/place-of-business address and resident agent. 3) Apply to the Gibraltar Income Tax Office for a corporate Tax Identification Number using the prescribed corporate registration form, attaching the constitutional documents, board resolution appointing a Gibraltar tax representative, and evidence of the place of business. 4) Continue with annual company registry validation, tax returns, and economic substance records if any taxable nexus exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (Gibraltar classification: non-resident offshore company; the Bermuda Exempted Company is subject to territorial taxation only on Gibraltar-source income. It is not subject to Gibraltar income tax on worldwide profits and is not a pass-through entity; any Gibraltar-source corporate profit is taxed at entity level at the standard company rate of 10%).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or general pass-through election exists in Gibraltar. The Bermuda Exempted Company is a juridical corporation and cannot elect transparent treatment. Under Bermuda law, it holds and maintains a certificate of exemption under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966, securing tax-exempt status in Bermuda. For hybrid mismatch purposes, the UK TIOPA 2010 Part 6A anti-hybrid rules may apply to the cross-border structure, but Gibraltar does not provide a unilateral hybrid classification election; treatment follows the entity's legal constitution and actual management and control.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Gibraltar: no VAT/GST/sales-and-use tax; limited indirect taxes consist mainly of customs import duties, excise duties on specified goods (alcohol, tobacco, petroleum), and stamp/registration duties. Online retail sales of automotive aftermarket parts from Gibraltar therefore carry no Gibraltar indirect tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable; Gibraltar imposes no turnover-based indirect-tax registration threshold because it has no general consumption tax. If the seller holds inventory in the UK or otherwise exceeds UK VAT registration thresholds, UK VAT registration may be required (standard UK VAT threshold GBP 90,000, or lower distance-selling thresholds).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None in Gibraltar; no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, API clearance, or mandatory e-invoicing regime applies. Commercial invoices and customs declarations must be retained for customs and tax verification. If the entity registers for UK VAT, UK HMRC Making Tax Digital requires digital VAT record-keeping and compatible software, but no live fiscal invoice clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: No Gibraltar VAT is levied, so there is no origin VAT output tax to zero-rate; exports from Gibraltar are outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect tax provided the goods physically leave Gibraltar and documentary evidence of export is retained. If the same Bermuda Exempted Company supplies goods from UK inventory, UK VAT zero-rating under VATA 1994 s.30 applies to direct exports to customers outside the UK, subject to export within the statutory time limit (normally three months) and retention of full export evidence. Offshore digital or ancillary services supplied to non-UK/non-Gibraltar business customers may be outside the scope of UK VAT under the place-of-supply rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Gibraltar Customs Export Declaration or export notification (including any Single Administrative Document requirement at the applicable frontier)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical removal from Gibraltar
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank receipt/SWIFT MT103 evidencing payment and repatriation of export proceeds
Certificate of origin or preferential origin documentation where a trade agreement preference is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under Gibraltar customs legislation, false or misleading export declarations attract monetary penalties, seizure/forfeiture of goods, and potentially imprisonment up to 2 years for deliberate evasion. Where UK VAT zero-rating is claimed, HMRC may retrospectively claw back output VAT plus interest, assess civil penalties up to 100% of the tax for careless or deliberate inaccuracies, and pursue criminal penalties of up to 7 years imprisonment for fraudulent evasion or fraudulent zero-rating claims. The retrospective assessment window is normally 6 years, extended to 20 years in cases of fraud or deliberate non-disclosure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Government of Gibraltar – Currency Commissioner (sole issuer of Gibraltar pound); Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) as banking and exchange-control administrator; HM Treasury/Bank of England provides sterling monetary backstop because GIP is pegged 1:1 to GBP.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar applies full current and capital account convertibility with no central-planning exchange controls. GIP is freely convertible to GBP at par; bank accounts may be held in GIP, GBP, EUR, USD, and other major currencies. Profit remittance from a non-resident exempt company is unrestricted and not subject to withholding, but remitting banks require underlying trade or equity documentation for FX evaluation and AML source-of-funds checks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation. Export receipts from the online auto-parts retail trade may be retained indefinitely in their original currency. Mandatory conversion ratio is 0%; no timeline applies in Gibraltar. If proceeds are sent from third-party marketplaces, the bank will need merchant settlement reports to identify trade as opposed to fee flows.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Treasury Account with FX line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium as primary clearing rail. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Revolut Business, Airwallex, Payoneer) are not Gibraltar-licensed credit institutions and therefore cannot open domestic GIP settlement accounts or issue commercial letters of credit. After Brexit they have lost EU passporting rights into Gibraltar; they can act only as collection/payout agents through a licensed Gibraltar bank. Acceptable for marketplace payouts and small working-capital wallets, never for capital escrow or trade LC settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: GFSC-regulated banks require at least one natural-person director and one UBO to complete either a physical KYC interview at the bank or, where explicitly approved, a recorded video interview with device verification and notarised apostilled corporate documents. Remote opening is available only if the bank's compliance model supports electronic identification; private banks such as Turicum and EFG will normally require physical interview in Gibraltar. Bermuda Exempted Company records must be apostilled in Bermuda before submission.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bermuda Exempted Company with nominee director, bearer shares, or remote UBO concentration outside UK/EU
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificate of incorporation; certificate of good standing from the Bermuda Registrar of Companies; register of directors and register of members; statutory declaration that no bearer shares have ever been issued; passport and proof of address of the natural-person director and UBO; group ownership chart; company search report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume online auto-parts retail with transactions originating from high-risk or sanctions-adjacent countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe/PayPal merchant settlement and payout reports; customer KYC and IP-geolocation explanation; e-commerce website terms, refund policy, and chargeback history; denied-party screening and geo-blocking certificates; compliance with PCI DSS; record of required export customs documentation and tracking numbers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No economic substance in Gibraltar and no tangible operating footprint in the jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda economic substance return under the Bermuda Economic Substance Act; board minutes showing management decisions outside Gibraltar; updated group structure chart; transfer pricing documentation for cross-border inventory purchases; confirmation of no Gibraltar permanent establishment and, where relevant, UK or Bermuda tax residence certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a related company with opaque source of funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving the capital contribution, loan note, or subscription agreement; bank statements of the remitting treasury company; audited or unaudited parent financial statements; source-of-wealth questionnaire; explanation of intercompany debt/equity ratio; confirmation that the remitting entity is not a shell in a high-risk tax haven.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 from the Bermuda treasury company to the Gibraltar operational account at a GFSC-licensed bank. Payment purpose code must be 'EQUITY' or, under UK BOP classification, 'A010 – direct investment equity capital'; for loans use 'LEND' or 'A015 – intercompany loans'. Pre-credit verification includes: board resolution, source-of-funds statement, corporate KYC pack, and sanctions/PEP screening. The bank will credit only after the funds match the beneficiary name and registry number and the treasury desk confirms the transaction has real economic purpose; no third-party mismatch or cash-pool split instructions are allowed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments are cleared via SWIFT MT103 for settlement in GBP, EUR, or USD; large shipment-backed purchases above GBP 50,000 should use a Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP 600 with the presenting bank in the supplier's country. Payment against invoice, packing list, transport document, and certificate of origin keeps the chain audit-ready. For Chinese suppliers, SWIFT MT103 in CNY/RMB with purpose code for trade in goods is acceptable; split settlements through non-bank fintechs are prohibited for treasury-account disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards with real underlying trade exposure
FX swaps (tom-next and spot-forward) for working-capital liquidity
Cross-currency swaps matching EUR, GBP, and USD liability streams
Vanilla FX options purchased to cap conversion costs on known settlement flows
NDFs for non-convertible emerging-market currencies, only where the bank has an approved line and the exposure is trade-backed

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
